Changelog

mrpipeline 0.8.0

New features

  • run_mr() and run_coloc() accept a lazy dplyr table for exposure and outcome as well as a data frame: a dplyr::tbl() on a DuckDB connection (via dbplyr), or any backend that supports filter() and collect(), such as an Arrow dataset query. Each function filters in the backend and collects only the rows it uses: the instruments, the outcome at those rsIDs, about 1000 SNPs for the allele orientation check, or the colocalization window. A genome-wide GWAS can therefore stay on disk instead of being loaded into memory on every call. Results are identical to the data-frame path, and a test pins this on the bundled data (#42).

  • For two lazy tables on the same database connection, the allele orientation check intersects the exposure and outcome rsIDs inside the database. Tables on different connections, or a data frame paired with a lazy table, still work, but each rsID column is collected into R for the intersect. verbose = TRUE reports when that happens.

  • DBI, dbplyr and duckdb are suggested packages only. mrpipeline installs and runs on data frames without them. Opening the database is up to the caller; see Large GWAS: lazy tables in the user guide.

Performance

  • The allele orientation check intersects the shared rsIDs with dplyr::intersect()/dplyr::setdiff() on one-column tibbles rather than base intersect()/setdiff() on vectors. That is about 6x faster for data-frame inputs too (vctrs set operations; benchmarked on 10M rsIDs).
